import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/test_9.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and types
target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
target_dtypes = {
    'admit': int,
    'gre': int,
    'gpa': float,
    'prestige': int
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    # Read CSV with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    
    # Ensure columns are exactly the target columns
    # (According to the prompt, all source schemas are identical to target schema)
    df = df[target_columns]
    
    # Enforce correct dtypes to match target schema
    df = df.astype(target_dtypes)
    
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Union all source tables by concatenation
# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target, union is appropriate
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: Export the combined DataFrame to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_63/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
